blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — barcode medication administration
stem: What is the primary medication-safety function of barcode medication administration (BCMA)?

options.A: Scan the medication and patient identifiers at the point of care to electronically verify the intended medication-patient match and record administration.
options.B: Replace the nurse's clinical assessment and independent safety checks because a successful barcode scan confirms that administration is clinically appropriate.
options.C: Verify medications mainly during pharmacy stocking while leaving bedside patient identification and medication matching to manual workflow.
options.D: Serve mainly as a documentation and billing tool, with medication-error prevention occurring through separate systems rather than bedside scanning.

rationale: A is correct. AHRQ describes BCMA as a point-of-care technology that uses barcode labeling of patients, medications, and medication records to electronically link the right medication/dose to the right patient and reduce administration errors. It can also link administration to the electronic medication administration record. B overstates the technology and ignores the need for nursing judgment and safe workflow. C omits the bedside patient-medication check. D mischaracterizes BCMA as primarily administrative rather than a medication-safety technology.
educational_objective: Explain how BCMA supports point-of-care patient-medication verification and medication-administration error prevention without replacing nursing judgment.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ); NCSBN
source_document_title: Medication Administration Errors; The Role of Bar Coding and Smart Pumps in Safety; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Current AHRQ PSNet medication-administration resources live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: AHRQ Medication Administration Errors, High Tech Solutions/Barcode medication administration: medication scanning supports the right medication; patient armband scanning supports right patient; BCMA electronically links the right dose/right medication to the right patient and reduces errors, while workarounds can degrade effectiveness. AHRQ Bar Coding perspective: BCMA provides point-of-care verification and can electronically record administration in the eMAR.
source_claim_supported: AHRQ directly supports BCMA as point-of-care electronic verification linking patient and medication identifiers to reduce medication-administration errors; it is not a substitute for safe clinical workflow.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control / medication-safety activities: use technology and safe medication-administration systems to prevent errors.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — relevant official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan medication-safety content was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; BCMA claims rely on current AHRQ HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; accurately describes point-of-care patient-medication verification and administration recording.
option_audit.B: Plausible automation overreliance but BCMA does not replace clinical judgment or other safety checks.
option_audit.C: Plausible pharmacy-use framing but omits BCMA's core bedside verification role.
option_audit.D: Plausible informatics misconception but BCMA is specifically intended to reduce medication-administration errors.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are similar in detail and professional tone; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
